enhanced.fullText:
The Pennsylvania Uniform Crime Reporting Act (PUCRA), codified at 18 Pa.C.S. § 9101 et seq., establishes mandatory crime reporting requirements for all law enforcement agencies within Pennsylvania, including campus police departments at higher education institutions. This state-level reporting requirement operates in conjunction with federal Clery Act obligations under 20 U.S.C. § 1092(f) and 34 CFR Part 668, creating a comprehensive framework for campus crime transparency and public safety.

Under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9103, Pennsylvania colleges and universities with sworn police officers must submit monthly Uniform Crime Reports (UCR) to the Pennsylvania State Police within ten days of each month's conclusion. The reporting encompasses Part I offenses including murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny-theft, motor vehicle theft, and arson, as well as arrest data for Part II offenses such as drug violations, weapons charges, and liquor law violations as specified in 18 Pa.C.S. § 9104.

Higher education institutions fall within the Act's scope when they operate certified police departments under 22 Pa. Code § 1-3. Campus security departments without arrest powers are exempt from PUCRA but remain subject to federal Clery Act requirements. The Pennsylvania State Police Bureau of Records and Identification serves as the central repository for all UCR data pursuant to 18 Pa.C.S. § 9105.

Compliance obligations extend beyond basic crime statistics to include detailed incident reporting through the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) format, as mandated by amendments effective January 2021. Institutions must report geographic information, victim demographics, offense circumstances, and property details for each incident occurring within their jurisdiction.

Enforcement mechanisms include potential loss of state funding for non-compliant institutions under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9106. The Pennsylvania State Police may conduct compliance audits and require remedial reporting for institutions demonstrating persistent non-compliance. Civil penalties range from $1,000 to $10,000 per month for continued violations.

Recent legislative updates in Act 16 of 2020 enhanced reporting requirements for sexual offenses and hate crimes, aligning state requirements more closely with federal Title IX obligations under 34 CFR Part 106. These amendments specifically impact higher education institutions by requiring enhanced demographic reporting and bias incident documentation.
enhanced.summary: Pennsylvania's Uniform Crime Reporting Act requires higher education institutions with sworn police departments to submit monthly crime statistics to state authorities within ten days of month-end, encompassing detailed incident data.
enhanced.requirements:
## Crime Data Reporting
- Submit monthly UCR reports within 10 days of month conclusion per 18 Pa.C.S. § 9103
- Report all Part I offenses occurring within institutional jurisdiction
- Include arrest data for Part II offenses including drug, weapon, and liquor violations
- Utilize NIBRS format for detailed incident reporting as of January 2021

## Institutional Coverage
- Applies to institutions operating certified police departments under 22 Pa. Code § 1-3
- Campus security without arrest powers exempt from PUCRA requirements
- Coordinate reporting with federal Clery Act obligations

## Data Quality Standards
- Provide geographic location details for each reported incident
- Include victim demographics and offense circumstances
- Document bias incidents and hate crime classifications per Act 16 of 2020
- Maintain accuracy standards subject to Pennsylvania State Police audit
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Monthly UCR reports due within 10 days of each month's end to Pennsylvania State Police Bureau of Records. NIBRS-format incident reports required for all qualifying offenses. Enhanced sexual offense and hate crime reporting required under Act 16 of 2020 amendments.
